title: Certified convex reconstruction and kernel exclusion for central configurations
oneLine: Exact certificates separate a uniquely reconstructed metric from a genuine gravitational central configuration—and exclude two whole seven-body parameter boxes.
abstract: This methods candidate develops quantitative and certified refinements of classical fixed-support convex reconstruction for central configurations. It gives an explicit Gram-matrix separation estimate in complete-kernel projector distance, primal–dual reconstruction error bounds, and a bounded 41-chart reduction retaining every possible stress rank for spatial seven-body configurations. Exact arithmetic certifies 54 local metric reconstructions and parameter patches, 15 higher-rank exclusion regions, and two full-dimensional singular-fibre boxes with noncentral rank-one PSD optimizers. The qualitative convex reconstruction and kernel-rigidity mechanism is attributed to Yoccoz and Albouy. The planar-eight and spatial-seven inventories remain lower bounds of twenty, not complete classifications.
narration: How much of a gravitational shape can be recovered from a matrix describing its forces? A central configuration is an arrangement in which every body's gravitational acceleration points towards the centre of mass with the same proportionality factor. These special shapes organise important motions in the many-body problem. This paper studies a way to search for them through smaller spaces of possible shapes. Classical work by Yoccoz and Albouy provides the starting point: a strictly convex reconstruction problem has at most one answer on a fixed support. The present candidate does not claim that classical mechanism as a discovery. Its contribution is quantitative and computational. It gives explicit reconstruction bounds and exact certificates that can reject entire regions of possible force kernels. One distinction is especially important. A uniquely reconstructed metric need not describe a central configuration. In two seven-body parameter boxes, the certified optimum has rank one: all the bodies lie on a line. Yet its forces do not satisfy the central-configuration equations. A positive constrained-optimisation slack supplies an additional witness that the proposed complete kernel cannot be realised. These are whole-box results, not just checks at the middle of a box. The evidence package also contains fifty-four local reconstruction certificates and fifteen regions excluding configurations of higher dimension. A twelve-stage exact replay and a supplied, separately written checking implementation have been run. That is inspectable computational evidence, not authenticated independent reproduction or a formal proof-assistant result. The remaining limitation is substantial: the paper does not enumerate every planar eight-body or spatial seven-body configuration, and it establishes no solver speedup. This is Evidence Press, certified convex reconstruction for central configurations, released on the first of October twenty twenty-six. The paper, code and evidence are linked on this page. This synthetic AI voice is an explanation, not additional scientific evidence.

problem.name: Certified reconstruction and exclusion in central-configuration searches

keyResults: Explicit quantitative separation of normalized central Gram matrices by complete-kernel projector distance, with fixed masses and stated distance bounds.
A semidefinite-constrained dual with a factorized gap and certified reconstruction errors, including the closed PSD boundary.

Two rational seven-body kernel-chart boxes, of dimensions eight and five and half-width 2^−34, have unique rank-one noncentral PSD optimizers throughout; neither box contains a realizable complete kernel.
54 local reconstruction and parameter-patch certificates, 15 higher-rank exclusion regions, and a 41-chart domain reduction retaining the spatial-seven singular branches.
evidence: Written proofs; twelve-stage exact producer replay; rational and outward-rounded interval certificates; semantic rejection controls; separately supplied alternative checks replayed with provenance limitations.
statusDetail: Unrefereed methods candidate. Classical fixed-support convexity, qualitative kernel rigidity and cone optimality are not claimed as new. Local certificates do not establish exhaustive target counts, global thickness, a complete singular-branch classification or solver speedup. Supplied reviewer independence is unauthenticated.

relatedWorks.citation: Yoccoz (1986), Description conjecturale des configurations centrales dans le problème planaire des 4 corps, §1.5, pp.2–3. Classical affine reduction, strict convexity and the distinction between positive distances and positive metrics.

Albouy (1997), Recherches sur le problème des N corps, Part 5, §§2.4 and 2.9, p.77. Fixed-support convex uniqueness is the decisive antecedent; qualitative complete-kernel rigidity follows from this framework.

Moczurad and Zgliczyński (2019), Central configurations in planar n-body problem with equal masses for n=5,6,7. The complete planar-seven catalogue is an external premise of the seven-body boundary application.

Chenciner (2016), Non-avoided crossings for n-body balanced configurations in R³ near a central configuration, Lemma 1. Reconstruction from the full force operator, distinct from comparing complete kernels.
Dias (2026), Brehm–Wintner–Conley dimension, Plücker coordinates, and generalized Dziobek–Williams equations. Actual-rank stratification and the complete-kernel Grassmannian invariant.
Albouy and Sun (2025), On the eigenvalues of a central configuration. Spectral context, including the classical collinear separation attributed to Conley; not a global seven-body spectral theorem.
